column2: Some in government argue that a small, fragmented nation cannot simply drift into empire the way old unified Britain once did -- it must commit to colonial expansion as a deliberate national project, or be crowded out entirely by rivals doing the same.
Committing treasury and shipwrights to a proper colonial fleet base will let the nation project and supply colonists far further afield than its merchant marine alone ever could.
The first colonial squadron has proven its worth. Expanding it further would let the nation contest more distant colonial ground against rival powers.
